newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Spicers sees better fine paper prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Spicers sees better fine paper prices.

text.p: Spicers Paper Ltd said on Monday it anticipated steadily rising fine paper prices and a more positive demand environment for the second half of its financial year to June 30, 1997.

"Moderate price increases implemented early in the current financial year in Europe for a number of fine paper grades appear to have gripped," the company's managing director Peter Hammond said in a statement.
Hammond said fine paper prices appeared to have bottomed out during the April-June quarter of 1996.

"Although a major recovery in market demand is yet to occur, we would epect sales and profit for the first half of 1996/97 to show an improvement on the previous six months, while remaining below the result for the corresponding period of 1995/96," Hammond said.

Spicers earlier said its net profit for the year to June 30 fell 35 percent to A$16.02 million from A$24.6 million in the previous year. The company said its fall in earnings reflected lower international paper prices.
"The price collapse was a world-wide phenomenon, not restricted simply to Spicers' geographic markets," Spicers said.
Spicers said its sales for the year were slightly higher at A$1.04 billion.
"Adjusting for the impact of price deflation, sales reflected market share gains in Australia and the maintenance of market shares in New Zealand and the United States," it said.
At 12.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), Spicers' shares were two cents weaker at A$2.15.
